summary: Butler County, AL former lookout site administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission; the register says only the stands remain.

facts.status_note: Former Fire Lookout Sites says the stands are all that remain of the tower

events.note: Registered September 18, 2019; nominated by Andrew Zerbe

evidence.supports: administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
the stands are all that remain; no public access described
evidence.quote: Stands are all that remain of the tower.

evidence.supports: opinion piece: at one time over 200 towers dotted Alabama
evidence.quote: at one time, over 200 of these artifacts dotted Alabama

evidence.supports: usual explanation: aircraft spot fires over a broader area than a 100-foot tower
evidence.quote: The most common explanation is that aircraft was more efficient in spotting fires in a much broader area than a 100-foot tower could provide

evidence.supports: probably fewer than 75 historic towers still standing in Alabama
evidence.quote: there are probably less than 75 of these historic structures still standing in Alabama

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: Only the FFLOS register entry describes this site. No build date, design, staffing or fire history was found in the register or in the two searches run. The 'stands' wording does not say which parts remain. Kaufmann is a statewide opinion piece, used only for context, not for this tower. A 'Chapman Lookout' in Butler County appeared in a search answer; it was not read and is not linked to this site. Searches used: 2 (one websearch.py fallback, one WebSearch). Page reads: FFLOS page, Kaufmann article, Wikipedia list (no Starlington entry).
